chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah the Exalted support him) informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (AS): 'A man urinated and had no water with him.' He said: 'He should squeeze from the base of his penis to its tip three squeezes, and shake its tip. If anything comes out after that, it is not from urine — rather it is from the seminal vessels (al-haba'il).'
As for what al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa — he said:
A man wrote to him: 'Is wudu (ritual ablution) obligatory from what exits from the penis after istibra'?' He wrote back: 'Yes.'

The [correct] interpretation of this narration is to take it as [indicating] a type of recommendation (istihbab) rather than obligation (wujub). Then he [the Sheikh], may Allah the Exalted support him, said: 'He should pour water over his right [hand] before inserting it into the vessel, washing it twice.' We shall discuss this matter later, God willing. Then he said: 'Then he inserts it — meaning the hand — into it [the vessel] and takes from it water for istinja'. He pours it onto the place of defecation (makhraj al-najw) and performs istinja' with his left hand.' That which indicates [this ruling follows…]

key_terms.الِاسْتِبْرَاءُ: istibra': ritual practice of clearing residual urine/fluid from the urethra after urination
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابُ: istihbab: legal category of recommendation (mustahabb); a meritorious but non-obligatory act
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: istinja': ritual cleansing of the private parts after urination or defecation
key_terms.الْحَبَائِلُ: al-haba'il: seminal vessels/ducts; post-istibra' discharge distinct from urine that does not invalidate wudu

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Baqir (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, how is istibra' performed without water, and is wudu obligatory or merely recommended for discharge that appears after istibra'?
ai.summary: This passage from Tahdhib al-Ahkam records Imam al-Baqir's (AS) ruling on istibra' (post-urination cleansing): when water is unavailable, the man squeezes from the base to the tip of the penis three times and shakes the tip; anything that emerges after this is not urine but from the seminal vessels (al-haba'il) and does not require renewed wudu. A corroborating narration via al-Saffar records a written query to the Imam on wudu after istibra', to which the Imam replied 'Yes'; Sheikh al-Tusi (the author) reconciles the two narrations by interpreting the second as indicating recommendation (istihbab) rather than strict obligation (wujub), and appends instructions from Sheikh al-Mufid on washing the right hand before drawing water from a vessel for istinja'.
